impulse-s1.title: A ball bounces off a wall
impulse-s1.html: The ball has a mass of 0.20 kg. Take right as positive.

impulse-s2.title: Momentum of a cart
impulse-s2.text: A motion sensor records the momentum of a 0.50 kg cart on a level track while a student pushes and then lets go. Positive is to the right.

items.q: Use the graph to find the impulse the wall exerts on the ball. Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the area of a rectangle. The graph is a triangle: area = ½ × base × height.
Value: the time is in milliseconds. 4 ms = 0.004 s.

why.correct: Impulse = area under F-t = ½(0.0040 s)(600 N) = 1.2 N·s, to the right.

items.q: What is the ball's change in momentum, in kg·m/s? Include the sign.

mistakes.why: Value: the initial velocity is to the left, so it is −4.0 m/s. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) = 0.20(2.0 − (−4.0)).

why.correct: Δp = m v_f − m v_i = (0.20)(+2.0) − (0.20)(−4.0) = +1.2 kg·m/s, matching the impulse: J = Δp.

items.q: What is the average force of the wall on the ball during the 4.0 ms contact, in newtons?

mistakes.why: Value: 600 N is the peak force. The average over a triangle is half the peak: J/Δt.

why.correct: F_avg = J/Δt = 1.2 N·s / 0.0040 s = 3.0 × 10² N, half the peak, as expected for a triangle.

items.q: A softer ball with the same mass and the same speeds before and after stays in contact for 8.0 ms instead. How does the wall's force compare?
options: Same impulse, half the average force
Twice the impulse, same average force
Same impulse, same average force
Half the impulse, half the average force

why.correct: J = F_avg Δt = Δp. Δp is the same, so doubling Δt halves F_avg. This is how airbags and helmets work.
options: Right: Δp is unchanged, so J is the same, spread over twice the time.
The impulse equals Δp, which has not changed.
Spreading the same impulse over more time lowers the average force.
The impulse is fixed by the change in momentum, 1.2 N·s.

items.q: A clay ball of the same mass and speed hits the wall and sticks. How does the impulse on it compare with the bouncing ball's?
options: Larger, because the clay comes to a full stop
Smaller: 0.80 N·s instead of 1.2 N·s
The same, because the incoming momentum is the same
Zero, because the clay ends at rest

why.correct: Clay: Δp = 0 − (−0.80) = +0.80 kg·m/s. Bouncing ball: +1.2 kg·m/s. A bounce needs more impulse than a stop.
options: Stopping is a smaller change than reversing. Bouncing needs extra impulse to send the ball back.
Right: the clay's Δp is 0 − (0.20)(−4.0) = 0.80 kg·m/s; bouncing back adds more.
The impulse depends on the final momentum too.
Ending at rest still means a change in momentum from −0.80 kg·m/s to 0.

items.q: What is the net force on the cart between 0 and 3.0 s, in newtons?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the change in momentum. The net force is the slope: Δp/Δt.

why.correct: F_net = slope of p-t = (1.2 − 0) kg·m/s / 3.0 s = 0.40 N.

items.q: What is the net force on the cart from 3.0 s to 5.0 s?
options: 1.2 N, the momentum value
0.40 N, the same as during the push
Zero, because the momentum is constant
Negative, because the cart is slowing

why.correct: F_net = Δp/Δt. From 3.0 s to 5.0 s, Δp = 0, so the net force is zero and the cart coasts at 2.4 m/s.
options: The force is the slope, not the height of the graph.
The slope changed to zero when the student let go.
Right: a flat p-t graph has zero slope, so F_net = 0.
The momentum is constant, so the cart is not slowing.

items.q: What is the cart's speed at 4.0 s, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that multiplies by the mass. Divide instead: v = p/m.

items.q: Which graph of net force against time matches the momentum graph?
options: Rising from 0 to 1.2 N over 3.0 s, then constant
Zero from 0 to 3.0 s, then 1.2 N
A constant 0.40 N for the whole 5.0 s
0.40 N from 0 to 3.0 s, then zero

why.correct: F_net is the slope of p against t: 0.40 N while p rises steadily, then 0 when p levels off.
options: That copies the shape of the p-t graph instead of taking its slope.
The force acts while p changes, from 0 to 3.0 s, not after.
After 3.0 s the momentum is constant, so the force is zero.
Right: each value is the slope of the p-t graph over that interval.

items.q: A tennis racket exerts an average force of 250 N on a ball for 0.0060 s. What impulse does it deliver, in N·s?

mistakes.why: Value: impulse is force times time, not force divided by time.

items.q: A 0.058 kg tennis ball arrives at 30. m/s and leaves the racket at 40. m/s in the opposite direction. What is the size of the impulse on the ball, in N·s?

mistakes.why: Value: you subtracted speeds. The velocities have opposite signs: Δv = 40 − (−30) = 70 m/s.

why.correct: Take the leaving direction as positive: Δp = (0.058)(+40.) − (0.058)(−30.) = 4.1 kg·m/s, so |J| = 4.1 N·s.

items.q: Why does bending your knees when you land from a jump reduce the force on your legs?
options: It lengthens the stopping time, so the same change in momentum needs a smaller average force
It reduces your change in momentum
It reduces your kinetic energy before landing
It reduces the impulse the ground gives you

why.correct: The impulse to stop you is fixed (J = Δp). Bending your knees spreads it over a longer time, so F_avg = J/Δt is smaller.
options: Right: F_avg = Δp/Δt.
You go from the same speed to rest either way, so Δp is the same.
Your speed at touchdown is set by the jump height, not by your knees.
The impulse equals Δp, which is the same either way.

items.q: The same average force acts on a cart for three times as long. The change in the cart's momentum becomes
options: 9 times as large
3 times as large
one third as large
the same

why.correct: Δp = F_avg Δt ∝ Δt, so tripling Δt triples Δp.
options: Nothing is squared in F_avg Δt.
Right: Δp = F_avg Δt.
More time with the same force gives a larger impulse, not smaller.
The momentum change grows with the time the force acts.

items.q: On a graph of force against time, what represents the impulse?
options: The slope of the curve
The highest force on the graph
The area under the curve
The time at which the force is largest

why.correct: Impulse J = area under F against t. On a p-t graph, the slope is the net force.
options: The slope is a rate of change of force, not an impulse.
A peak force says nothing about how long it acted.
Right: impulse is the sum of F Δt over the interval.
Impulse needs force and time together.

items.q: An egg dropped onto a pillow is compared with the same egg dropped from the same height onto a hard floor (where it stops sooner). Predict how each pillow value compares with the floor value.

variables.name: The egg's change in momentum
variables.why: It arrives at the same speed and stops in both cases.

variables.name: The impulse on the egg
variables.why: Impulse equals the change in momentum.

variables.name: The average force on the egg
variables.why: The same impulse is spread over a longer time on the pillow.

why.correct: J = Δp is the same; F_avg = J/Δt is smaller on the pillow because the stop takes longer.
